title: Protect short analytics from long-running work
description: Change dashboard arrivals, concurrent ETL work, and queue policy. The model exposes slot demand, admitted capacity, queue pressure, and eligible scaling as separate signals.

profiles.label: Steady mixed workload
profiles.detail: Moderate dashboard traffic shares the warehouse with a small batch.

profiles.label: Morning dashboard burst
profiles.detail: Business users arrive together while the overnight ETL tail is still active.

profiles.label: Month-end contention
profiles.detail: A dashboard burst overlaps many resource-intensive transformations.

policies.label: One undifferentiated queue
policies.detail: Dashboard work receives only the base slots left after admitted ETL queries.
policies.consequence: A shared queue is simple, but long work can consume the same admission capacity needed by short interactive queries.

policies.label: Separate BI and ETL queues
policies.detail: Reserve 42% of base slots for dashboards and route ETL to the remaining capacity.
policies.consequence: Routing and priority protect dashboard admission, while ETL can queue when its reserved base capacity is full.

policies.label: Isolation plus concurrency scaling
policies.detail: Keep queue boundaries and allow up to six modeled eligible dashboard slots beyond the base cluster.
policies.consequence: Eligible work can leave the base queue, but scaling is not a substitute for query limits, routing, or measuring usage and cost.
